messages:
lina: Hey — saw a weird one in prod-preview. Tenant `org-42` dashboard export included a panel widget that belongs to `org-7`. Not just UI flash, the CSV had rows with org-7 ids. :grimacing:
sam: ugh. any repro steps?
lina: open any dashboard for org-42 -> click Export CSV -> inspect first widget block. Happened on 3 different users.
jon: do we have any recent changes to the panel registry or export pipeline?
emily: rollout of `panel-fast-path` yesterday touched prefetch + registry caching. Canary only, but maybe rollout percent higher in preview.
kevin: can you paste the network trace or the internal api call? which endpoint returned the widget?
lina: trace shows call to `/internal/panels/resolve` with header `x-org: org-42` but response payload had `org_id: org-7` in widget.metadata. Response looked like it came from cache.
sam: that screams cache key not namespaced. I bet the cache key is just `panel:${widget_id}` instead of `panel:${org_id}:${widget_id}`.
emily: checked service logs — `panel-lookup` emits cache.get keys: `panel:9423` for multiple orgs. Confirmed.
jon: so root cause = registry cache keys omit org. Quick mitigation?
kevin: disable panel prefetch for the export route, roll back canary, or invalidate cache entries with a script.
lina: prefer quick rollback of `panel-fast-path` canary to 0% for preview env, then schedule a patch.
emily: telemetry note: our panel metrics don't include org tag, so this leakage was invisible in grouping. We need org dimension on `panel.resolve.cache_hit`.
sam: agree. Long term we should require that all internal cache layers take an `org_id` token and include it in key derivation.
jon: debate: fix at cache layer vs fix at caller (ensure callers add org prefix). I'm leaning cache-layer defensive (always require namespacing).
kevin: cache-layer fix is safer but riskier change; callers might already rely on current behavior. We should also add a runtime assertion that rejects non-namespaced keys in production for a short window.
emily: for telemetry we can add a new gauge `panel.resolve.orgless_hits` to detect callers still emitting non-namespaced keys.
lina: plan: 1) rollback canary in preview now (kevin/ops?) 2) run invalidation script to remove `panel:*` keys older than 24h in preview 3) patch cache library to enforce org namespace + add metrics 4) coordinate rollout with devops 5) add regression test for export CSV to ensure widget org matches dashboard org
kevin: rolling rollback now — dev-deploy-bot should post once done.
dev-deploy-bot: deploy rollback triggered for service `panel-lookup`, env=preview, target=canary->0%, started by kevin at 1711114478.
kevin: invalidation script ready, will run after rollback completes — script erases keys matching `panel:*` in preview redis (we'll constrain to last 48h).
jon: I'll own the cache library patch and add an opt-in compatibility flag for callers, plus a lint rule for caller libs.
emily: I'll add the telemetry change and a dashboard showing org-scoped hits. Also add an alert if orgless hits > 0.5%
sam: adding an e2e test in dashboard-export suite now.
lina: thanks team. post-mortem notes: discuss requiring org in internal API contract, add API contract tests for internal routes.
kevin: rollback done, dev-deploy-bot posted.
dev-deploy-bot: rollback completed for `panel-lookup` canary->0% at 1711114502, healthchecks OK.
lina: running repro now — export CSV looks clean in preview for the repro users.
emily: pushed telemetry change to staging branch; will merge after tests.
jon: starting on cache patch PR. assigning reviewers: sam, kevin.
sam: quick question — quotas? could this leak have allowed org-42 to see usage/metrics of org-7?
emily: looks limited to panel metadata + small widget payloads. No token or billing data leaked. But we should audit logs for any access to sensitive fields.
kevin: ok, I'm going to run the redis invalidation and capture before/after stats.
lina: great. follow up sync in #eng-platform in 1h for roll-forward plan. :eyes:
